Stripe's Customer Success Managers (CSM) oversee the post-sales lifecycle for Stripe users, ensuring they realize the maximum value of their investment. This partnership drives user success, increases retention and expansion, and supports mutually beneficial renewal outcomes. Few roles provide such a direct impact on the growth of the company.

What you’ll do

The Customer Success Manager for Radar is a specialized scaled coverage role serving the Global CSM Team. You will work across account executives, technical account managers, ProServ, and AEPs to drive Radar adoption and deliver measurable improvements in fraud rates, dispute rates, and overall payments health. You will be the domain expert and operational backbone for Stripe’s fraud and disputes product suite (examples: Radar Standard, Radar for Fraud Teams (RFFT), Disputes, Adaptive 3DS, Smart Refunds, Radar for Multiprocessor, and Radar for Platforms, working across partners in Product, ProServ, Support, and Data Science.

The ideal candidate combines deep fraud and payments risk domain expertise with strong cross-functional instincts.

Responsibilities

  • Monitor and Mitigate Risk: Identify churn signals, integration gaps, and potential Card Brand Monitoring Program (CBMP) risks to proactively initiate optimization conversations.
  • Drive Value and Adoption: Educate users on fraud and disputes products, drive adoption of high-value features, and identify upsell opportunities
  • Cross-Functional Partnership: Collaborate with cross functional teams to support trials, conversions, and joint enablement.
  • Voice of the Customer: Act as the internal advocate by routing product feedback, representing user needs in roadmap discussions, and flagging systemic integration issues.
  • Operational Leadership: Own reporting and performance metrics, lead internal training, and participate in key customer business reviews (QBRs/EBCs)

Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

  • 5+ years of enterprise relationship management or consulting, with 2+ years embedded in payments fraud, risk management, or disputes at a payments company, bank, or fintech
  • Domain Expertise: Proven experience with fraud prevention, chargeback management, and risk operations, including familiarity with fraud patterns, friendly fraud, first-party misuse, and dispute representment
  • Product Fluency: Hands-on experience with machine learning-based fraud tools, rule-based fraud engines, or dispute management platforms; familiarity with Stripe Radar is a strong plus
  • Executive Presence: Experience presenting fraud and risk performance data to and influencing senior stakeholders across risk, finance, and operations functions
  • Operational Rigor: Ability to manage a complex book of business, balancing multiple merchant fraud investigations, dispute escalations, and performance reviews simultaneously
  • Ability to navigate data and people to find answers, including interpreting fraud dashboards, dispute analytics, and authorization rate metrics

Preferred qualifications

  •  Deep fraud and payments risk domain expertise with strong cross-functional instincts.

title: Data Analyst, Intern
description:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a technology company focused on improving the conditions for economic growth and prosperity. We build programmable financial infrastructure, rethinking from first principles how financial services should work, to make it easier and cheaper for any business to start and scale. More than 10 million businesses build on Stripe, spanning the economic frontier—from solo founders to established enterprises—united by a practical focus on growth. The most ambitious companies in the world use Stripe as core infrastructure to grow faster. They process trillions of dollars a year on Stripe, equivalent to around 1.6% of global GDP. While economic growth makes everyone better off, open markets also enable greater variety. When any business can easily serve a global customer base, the quality and diversity of products in the world increase, and craft and creativity are unleashed into the smallest niches. Our own growth is wholly contingent on the success of the businesses building on Stripe. We therefore invest back into our technology at an unusual rate. We make upgrades to our products every single day to deliver compounding gains to our customers. We maintain some of the most reliable APIs on the internet. We build entirely new pieces of financial infrastructure to enable new ideas. And our significant advances in risk and fraud infrastructure over many years are making the internet economy safer and more accessible.

Though people at Stripe don’t tend to take themselves seriously, Stripe is a fairly serious place: our customers are depending on us for their livelihoods. We admire ambition, intensity, curiosity, humility, and rigor. The most effective people become knowledgeable about many domains besides their own. Any company is an applied exercise in understanding some aspect of society or the market. In working with so many (especially the new and innovative ones), we think that Stripe is one of the very best places to learn about how the world works.

 

About the team

Data Science at Stripe is a vibrant community where data analysts and data scientists learn and grow together. You'll work with some of the most fundamental data at Stripe, and use that data to help drive company-wide initiatives. We have a variety of Data Analytics roles and teams across Stripe and will seek to align you to the most relevant team based on your background.

 

What you’ll do

As an intern at Stripe you’ll work on projects across our stack that directly impact the way millions of businesses operate. You’ll own problems end to end with the support of your manager and teammates. It’s an opportunity to work alongside some of the most creative and technically rigorous data analysts and scientists in the industry. You'll partner deeply with teams across Stripe to ensure that our users, our products, and our business have the models, data products, and insights needed to make decisions and grow responsibly. You'll work closely with partners to extract insights from the rich and complex data at Stripe. You'll build metrics, scalable data pipelines, dashboards, and reports to inform and run the business. You'll deliver actionable business recommendations through analyses and data storytelling.

Our internship program is competitive and the expectations are high.

 

Responsibilities

  • Analyze data and running experiments to drive impact
  • Ensure that our users, our products, and our business have the models, data products, and insights needed to make decisions and grow responsibly
  • Create metrics, reports, and dashboards to inform and run the business
  • Extend Stripe’s metrics semantic layer
  • Build new data assets and improve existing data assets to support decision-making, products, and business processes
  • Assess the impact of decisions, product launches, and product improvements using business analytics and A/B testing
  • Learn quickly by asking great questions, finding how to work with your mentor and teammates effectively, and communicating the status of your work clearly
  • Present your work to the Data Science team, partner teams, and fellow interns

 

Who you are

  • Ambitious builder: You’re energized by building solutions without clear precedent and solving problems with far-reaching consequences. Successful Stripes are deeply curious, and prefer the joy of discovery to the comfort of certainty.
  • Rigorous thinker: You appreciate that things worth doing are rarely simple. You enjoy working on problems that have never been tackled before.
  • Adaptable problem solver: You adapt quickly and treat obstacles as opportunities. At Stripe we embrace kindness while encouraging Stripes to take measured risks and act boldly, even in the absence of consensus.

 

Minimum requirements

  • Enrolled in a quantitative Bachelor’s or Master's degree program (e.g. Data Analytics, Statistics, Economics, Mathematics, etc.) with the expectation of graduating in December 2027 or spring/summer 2028
  • Experience with SQL
  • Proficiency with AI tools to accelerate model development, analysis, and coding
  • Experience communicating and collaborating with multidisciplinary stakeholders in a team environment

 

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience writing and debugging data pipelines
  • Demonstrated ability to evaluate and receive feedback from mentors, peers, and stakeholders via experience from previous internships or other multi-person projects
  • Ability to learn new systems and form an understanding of those systems, through independent research and working with a mentor and subject matter experts

description:

We are hiring a senior editorial leader to help bring original stories and insights from Stripe–based on our data, expertise, and customer conversations–to a broader audience via media partnerships and other brand marketing channels. This person will be an exceptional editor, writer, and creative partner with strong instincts about what earns attention: an argument worth making, an unexpected angle, an elegant execution, or a piece of work that people genuinely want to share.

This is a senior individual contributor role reporting to the leader of Stripe’s Narrative & Editorial team. The role will spend most of its time shaping major external media partnerships, with the remainder split between helping with original editorial work and advising partner teams on new ideas and their execution.

Responsibilities

  • Lead the editorial and creative direction for Stripe’s most important external media partnerships, including advertising content, research-led collaborations, and original editorial programs developed with respected publishers and creators.
  • Develop work that feels native to the audience and editorial environment in which it appears—not generic brand messaging placed beside someone else’s work.
  • Turn Stripe’s original data analyses, economic insights, customer stories, and more into content pieces that are clear, surprising, useful, and memorable–and that readers and listeners won’t want to skip over.
  • Shape the full editorial process for partnership work: refining briefs, identifying the strongest ideas, directing creative development, and providing decisive feedback on drafts and final deliverables.
  • Direct and manage agencies, external creators, and editorial partners as needed, working within existing partnership structures and commercial agreements.
  • Write, edit, and materially improve high-stakes content across formats, including blog posts, newsletter segments, podcast scripts, ad copy, social posts, and more.
  • Generate original concepts for creative programs, editorial franchises, and nontraditional formats that broaden how Stripe contributes to conversations about the internet economy.
  • Serve as a trusted thought partner to teams across Stripe, helping them clarify ideas, find the strongest expression of their work, and make better creative decisions.
  • Partner with colleagues in Brand Marketing, Brand Design, Content Marketing, Portfolio PMM, Copywriting, and Customer Marketing to make Stripe’s storytelling more coherent and distinctive.
  • Define and uphold a clear quality bar for editorial and partnership work, making well-reasoned calls about what is ready to represent Stripe and what still needs improvement.

We are looking for someone with exceptional editorial judgment and a demonstrated ability to make complicated ideas compelling. You may have developed that experience in a newsroom, independent publication, creative studio, agency, research institution, technology company, or another rigorous creative environment.

  • You have 8+ years of relevant experience in editorial, writing, creative development, journalism, publishing, media, brand strategy, or a closely related field. This may include experience writing consistently for a large online followership, even if not professionally.

  • You are, in the best sense, very online: an active reader of and contributor to the newsletters, social platforms, and niche communities where people debate new ideas about technology, economics, science, business, and culture. You can spot emerging arguments, voices, and formats early—and engage with them authentically, with intellectual honesty and your own point of view.
  • You are an excellent editor. You can diagnose what is missing from a draft or idea, identify the most interesting argument, and give feedback that makes the work materially better.

You will help customers define not only what they want to build with Stripe, but also how they will achieve value from it.

What you’ll do

Own enterprise Professional Services opportunities

  • Own Professional Services bookings, pipeline creation, qualification, and forecasting across an assigned set of strategic enterprise accounts.
  • Partner with Account Executives and Solutions Architects on account plans that identify where Professional Services can accelerate adoption, reduce implementation risk, and unlock expansion.
  • Engage early in complex opportunities to shape the services strategy, customer value proposition, and path to implementation.
  • Build and maintain accurate forecasts, close plans, and stakeholder maps for complex, multi-party sales cycles.
  • Identify follow-on advisory, implementation, and transformation opportunities as customers expand their use of Stripe.

Lead discovery and shape practical solutions

  • Lead executive discovery sessions, assessments, and workshops with customer stakeholders across product, engineering, finance, operations, risk, security, and procurement.
  • Understand a customer’s business objectives, current environment, technical architecture, operating model, and implementation constraints.
  • Translate customer requirements into a practical services approach, including scope, assumptions, dependencies, milestones, risks, success measures, and an activation and realization plan.
  • Partner with Solutions Architecture, Product, Engineering, delivery teams, and external partners to validate feasibility and create solutions that are valuable to customers and deliverable by Stripe.
  • Advise senior customer leaders on business cases for digital transformation, platform adoption, operational efficiency, and new revenue opportunities.

Drive commercial execution

  • Create tailored proposals, pricing approaches, and Statements of Work for advisory, implementation, packaged, and phased transformation engagements.
  • Shape commercial models that balance customer outcomes, delivery confidence, scope clarity, and long-term Stripe adoption.
  • Lead negotiations with senior customer stakeholders, procurement, legal, and internal partners.
  • Manage scope, resourcing, dependencies, implementation risk, and customer expectations before work begins.
  • Apply strong commercial judgment to determine when a customer needs a focused assessment, a defined implementation package, a broader transformation roadmap, or partner-delivered support.

Connect sales to delivery and product strategy

  • Prepare delivery teams with clear customer context, business outcomes, decision history, risks, assumptions, and stakeholder expectations.
  • Maintain continuity from opportunity creation through customer kickoff and early delivery.
  • Partner with Customer Success, Delivery, and Support teams to help customers progress from signature to activation, adoption, and expansion.
  • Surface recurring enterprise customer needs and market insight to Product and Engineering teams to inform Stripe’s product strategy.
  • Contribute to repeatable sales plays, service offerings, tools, and best practices that improve how Stripe sells and delivers Professional Services.

AI and emerging technology

Stripe customers are increasingly evaluating AI-enabled products, automation, and new digital business models. You do not need to be an AI engineer or researcher, but you should be comfortable discussing how AI-related initiatives affect data readiness, integrations, security, privacy, governance, adoption, and implementation sequencing.

You will use AI-enabled tools responsibly to improve account research, solutioning, documentation, forecasting, and delivery visibility, while applying sound judgment and validating recommendations with the appropriate technical and delivery experts.

Who you are

You are an enterprise Professional Services seller who combines consultative sales, technical fluency, and delivery-aware commercial judgment. You can lead a customer from an initial business problem through discovery, solution shaping, proposal development, SOW negotiation, close, and delivery handoff.

You are comfortable with executives and technical teams alike. You can ask strong questions, translate technical possibilities into business outcomes, challenge assumptions constructively, and create clarity in ambiguous situations. You know that a successful services sale is not simply a signed SOW; it is a credible and measurable path to customer value.

Minimum requirements

  • 5+ years of experience selling Professional Services, consulting, implementation, managed services, or complex technology solutions to enterprise customers.
  • A track record of originating, shaping, and closing sizable services or transformation engagements.
  • Experience owning a services sales cycle from discovery through proposal, SOW development, negotiation, contract signature, and delivery handoff.
  • Experience leading executive-level discovery, workshops, assessments, or business-case conversations.
  • Ability to understand complex business and technical requirements and translate them into an executable services approach.
  • Experience partnering effectively with Account Executives, Solutions Architects, delivery teams, Product, Engineering, and external partners.
  • Strong commercial judgment across scope, pricing, assumptions, dependencies, risks, resourcing, and customer expectations.
  • Working knowledge of APIs, integrations, cloud-based platforms, data flows, and enterprise implementation considerations.
  • Ability to manage competing priorities, navigate ambiguity, and maintain a rigorous pipeline and forecast.

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience in payments, fintech, financial infrastructure, billing, marketplaces, money movement, fraud, risk, or digital commerce.
  • Experience selling to senior product, engineering, finance, operations, security, or technology leaders.
  • Experience with enterprise integrations, cloud adoption, APIs, platform implementations, data modernization, or digital transformation programs.
  • Experience selling packaged, phased, outcome-oriented, or partner-delivered services.
  • Familiarity with AI-enabled software or automation, including practical implementation questions around data, security, governance, adoption, and measurable business value.
  • Experience in a high-growth technology company, cloud provider, enterprise SaaS company, consulting firm, or systems integrator.

By analyzing data and preparing insights, you will inform decisions that maximize attendance and enhance the overall attendee experience. Strategy and concept development:

Technical Operations roles in Financial Connections are a dynamic and critical component of the organization's success. As Financial Connections TechOps Manager, you will lead a team of Integration Reliability Engineers who sit at the intersection of product and platform engineers, financial partners, and AI automation. Your role is to ensure that nothing is lost in translation: setting the standard for how the team operates, where it invests, and how the operational backbone of Stripe's open banking ecosystem stays reliable at scale.

What you'll do

Lead integration reliability and partner operations

  • Own the health of Financial Connections' banking integrations at the team level—define what "reliable" looks like across the partner ecosystem, set the operational bar, and hold the team to it
  • Serve as the management escalation point for complex partner issues, coordinating across financial partners, Stripe engineering, and product leadership with urgency and clear accountability
  • Drive strategy for integration health: set SLOs, own the operational metrics that surface risk before it becomes an incident, and ensure the team's priorities reflect the actual risk landscape
  • Prioritize the integration backlog in partnership with your team—new partner launches, reliability improvements, partner-driven technical changes—balancing operational urgency against longer-term investment
  • Sustain technical relationships with key financial partners at the leadership level, including commercial alignment, escalation frameworks, and forward-looking roadmap coordination

Shape the agentic automation strategy

  • Set direction for how the team applies LLM-powered agentic workflows to high-volume operational work—making deliberate choices about where automation creates leverage and where human judgment must remain in the loop
  • Partner with product and platform engineering to ensure agentic tooling investments are appropriately scoped, shipped reliably, and measurably reduce toil for the team over time
  • Build your team's capability to design and operate Human-in-the-Loop review systems—ensuring automation is deployed with the right safeguards, risk calibration, and operational ownership
  • Identify the manual, high-volume process categories that are ripe for elimination and sequence the work to deliver compounding leverage, not one-off fixes

Build and grow the TechOps function

  • Hire, onboard, and develop a team of TechOps Integration Reliability Engineers—your most important output is a highly capable, well-coached team that is genuinely energized by the mission
  • Build a team culture that values deep technical ownership, urgency and discipline in incident response, and a bias toward eliminating entire classes of problems rather than just resolving individual instances
  • Serve as the operational bridge between Financial Connections engineering leadership, partnerships, compliance, and legal—surfacing the team's needs and translating partner and regulatory requirements into clear engineering priorities
  • Represent TechOps in cross-functional planning cycles: make the operational implications of product decisions visible, advocate for reliability investments, and ensure the team's contributions are understood and valued across the org

Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

TechOps EM roles require a genuine command of both the people side of management and the technical domain. You need enough depth to evaluate your team's work credibly, set and hold a high bar for quality, and earn trust with financial partners and internal engineering partners alike. Successful candidates bring a track record of leading operational teams in complex, integration-heavy technical environments—and find genuine satisfaction in building a team and a function beyond solving individual problems.

Minimum requirements

  • Minimum 3+ years of people leadership experience in a TechOps team
  • Demonstrated people management experience with clear evidence of the fundamentals: coaching individuals to do their best work, navigating performance conversations, hiring well, and building a team that functions at a high level. Minimum 3 years of people leadership experience managing a TechOps team. 
  • Hands-on technical experience depth to lead the team's work credibly: you actively read and write code, investigate integration failures end-to-end, query data to scope and diagnose issues, and evaluate the quality of your team's technical decisions and output
  • Operational leadership experience: you've owned production reliability, incident command, and operational programs in a complex technical environment; you know how to build escalation paths, define SLOs, and drive urgency without creating unsustainable conditions for your team
  • Experience managing technical partner or vendor relationships at a leadership level: you've been the accountable point of contact for external parties and have navigated escalations, roadmap alignment, and commercial considerations
  • Strong written and verbal communication calibrated to both technical and non-technical audiences, including the ability to represent the team's priorities and operational posture to engineering and business leadership
  • Instinct to build leverage at the team level: you think about eliminating classes of problems through automation, tooling, and process—not just solving what's in front of you
  • Experience building or overseeing agentic or LLM-powered workflows in a production environment: either as a practitioner or as a manager who has led teams doing this work at meaningful scale

Preferred qualifications

  • Deep familiarity with open banking, financial data aggregation, or payments partner integrations: you understand the failure modes, the partner ecosystem dynamics, and the regulatory and compliance context that shapes this work
  • A track record of building TechOps or operations engineering teams: you've defined role shapes, built the hiring pipeline, leveled candidates, and grown a team from a foundational state

Bridge, acquired by Stripe in 2025 and operating as a Stripe subsidiary, is a stablecoin-powered payments platform built to simplify global money movement.

About the team

The Financial Crime, Compliance and Risk Oversight (FinCRO) Investigations Management team provides second-line-of-defence (2LoD) financial crime risk oversight and coordinates casework across Stripe’s EMEA region. The team manages user risk and synthesises investigative information into decision-ready analysis and intelligence for MLROs, RCOs, and other key stakeholders. It also identifies control weaknesses, coordinates complex investigations, and supports local examinations and inquiries from financial partners, law enforcement, and other external stakeholders.

What you’ll do

We are looking for a financial crime professional with Luxembourg- and EU-specific experience to join the EMEA Investigations Management team. Based in Luxembourg, you will focus primarily on Bridge Building S.A. while also supporting Stripe’s broader investigations work.

As an Investigator on the EMEA Investigations Management team, you will:

  • Review high-risk investigative casework and provide 2LoD oversight across a wide variety of financial crime risk types
  • Prepare and submit Luxembourg Suspicious Transaction Reports (STRs) to the Cellule de renseignement financier (CRF) for Bridge Building S.A., working closely with the MLRO and in line with established governance
  • Oversee local customer risk decisions for Bridge Building S.A., including matters escalated through country- or entity-specific risk management forums, in close partnership with the MLRO and Investigations Leads
  • Review high-risk sanctions investigations, such as potential matches against relevant regional lists, and handle related submissions
  • Use and evolve AI and agentic tools to enhance casework research and analysis, surface actionable intelligence, and improve investigative workflows while applying expert judgement and maintaining human oversight of risk decisions and regulatory filings
  • Assess casework to produce clear investigative analyses, intelligence briefs, and other decision-ready outputs that identify threats, support reporting workstreams, and inform MLROs, RCOs, and other stakeholders
  • Identify potential control gaps through casework analysis and recommend solutions to mitigate financial crime risks across the programme and in individual cases
  • Serve as a point of contact for investigation-related inquiries from law enforcement and FIUs, financial partners, auditors, and other external stakeholders
  • Demonstrate sound judgement and the ability to navigate complex, high-risk cases where the correct decision may not be immediately clear

Who you are

Minimum requirements

  • 3+ years of experience in investigative roles within financial crime, AML, risk, intelligence research, or a related field
  • Fluency in English and French
  • Demonstrated experience preparing regulatory disclosures, including direct experience with Luxembourg STR filings and goAML
  • A deep understanding of financial technologies, including payments, cryptocurrency, stablecoins, and Banking-as-a-Service products
  • Strong knowledge of Luxembourg and EU AML, terrorist financing, and sanctions regulations
  • Stakeholder management skills, including the ability to work effectively with MLROs and communicate complex risk decisions clearly
  • Excellent research and writing skills and the ability to produce concise, decision-ready investigative outputs
  • The ability to synthesise large amounts of information, including transaction data, using tools such as SQL, Excel, and AI
  • The ability to work efficiently and independently in a fast-paced environment

Preferred qualifications

title: Financial Data Analyst Intern, Technical Operations
job_title: Financial Data Analyst Intern, Technical Operations
description:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a technology company focused on improving the conditions for economic growth and prosperity. We build programmable financial infrastructure, rethinking from first principles how financial services should work, to make it easier and cheaper for any business to start and scale. More than 10 million businesses build on Stripe, spanning the economic frontier—from solo founders to established enterprises—united by a practical focus on growth. The most ambitious companies in the world use Stripe as core infrastructure to grow faster. They process trillions of dollars a year on Stripe, equivalent to around 1.6% of global GDP. While economic growth makes everyone better off, open markets also enable greater variety. When any business can easily serve a global customer base, the quality and diversity of products in the world increase, and craft and creativity are unleashed into the smallest niches. Our own growth is wholly contingent on the success of the businesses building on Stripe. We therefore invest back into our technology at an unusual rate. We make upgrades to our products every single day to deliver compounding gains to our customers. We maintain some of the most reliable APIs on the internet. We build entirely new pieces of financial infrastructure to enable new ideas. And our significant advances in risk and fraud infrastructure over many years are making the internet economy safer and more accessible. 

Though people at Stripe don’t tend to take themselves seriously, Stripe is a fairly serious place: our customers are depending on us for their livelihoods. We admire ambition, intensity, curiosity, humility, and rigor. The most effective people become knowledgeable about many domains besides their own. Any company is an applied exercise in understanding some aspect of society or the market. In working with so many (especially the new and innovative ones), we think that Stripe is one of the very best places to learn about how the world works.

About the team

The APAC Payments TechOps team ensures the accuracy of financial data flowing through Stripe's payment infrastructure, manages aging balances, maintains compliance with partner and regulatory requirements, and builds tooling to detect and resolve data quality issues at scale. Through the internship, you will work with real financial data, gain experience in payments data analysis and operational problem-solving, and have opportunities to present your work to your team and the wider org. Each intern has a dedicated intern manager, and every project is part of the team's roadmap and will directly help Stripe's mission.

What you’ll do

Every internship at Stripe centers around a real, legitimate project that our team urgently needs. We will support you in shipping it. Yes, you will actually ship it. Example projects include building data quality checks for payment flows, creating dashboards to surface aging balance trends, automating compliance reporting, or analyzing cost structures across partner networks. As a Stripe intern, you'll be tackling important projects while working alongside exceptional people who insist on doing their best work. You'll learn from people with high standards who are great at inspiring others to do more and go further. We value technical and personal growth, and see our internship program as a vehicle to foster both.

Responsibilities

  • Analyze financial data by writing queries and examining data quality, reconciliation accuracy, or cost structures across Stripe's payment flows
  • Write code or build tooling that will be used in production and has meaningful impact to Stripe's payment operations
  • Give and receive technical feedback through code reviews, data model discussions, or analysis walkthroughs
  • Collaborate with engineers, product managers, and finance stakeholders to seek and incorporate feedback on your work
  • Learn quickly by asking great questions, by working with your intern manager and teammates effectively, and by communicating the status of your work clearly

Who you are

  • Ambitious builder: You’re energized by building solutions without clear precedent and solving problems with far-reaching consequences. Successful Stripes are deeply curious, and prefer the joy of discovery to the comfort of certainty.
  • Rigorous thinker: You appreciate that things worth doing are rarely simple. You enjoy working on problems that have never been tackled before. 
  • Adaptable problem solver: You adapt quickly and treat obstacles as opportunities. At Stripe we embrace kindness while encouraging Stripes to take measured risks and act boldly, even in the absence of consensus.

Minimum requirements

  • A strong fundamental understanding of quantitative analysis through pursuit of a Bachelor's, Master's, or PhD degree in computer science, data science, finance, economics, information systems, or a related discipline
  • Some experience and familiarity with programming or data analysis, either through side projects or coursework. We work mostly in SQL, Python, and Ruby. We believe new programming languages can be learned if the fundamentals and general knowledge are present
  • Experience from previous internships or other multi-person projects, including open source contributions, that demonstrate evaluating and receiving feedback from mentors, peers, and stakeholders
  • Ability to learn unfamiliar systems and form an understanding of those systems, through independent research and working with a mentor and subject matter experts

Preferred qualifications

  • At least 2 years of university education, or equivalent work experience
  • Familiarity with SQL and querying relational databases, either through coursework or personal projects
  • Interest in payments, fintech, or financial systems
  • Comfort with developer tools (e.g. git) and data visualization
  • A strong interest in understanding how financial data flows through complex payment systems and ensuring its accuracy
  • Ability to write clearly to explain analytical findings to stakeholders, team members, and other Stripes

This team works closely with partner teams throughout the hardware and software product lifecycle, from hardware manufacturing to Android application teams.

title: Forward Deployed AI Accelerator, Marketing

description:

The Stripe Marketing organization is undergoing a fundamental transformation in how it works. We're building a team of Forward Deployed AI Accelerators (FDAs) embedded directly with marketing cohorts to make AI the default mode for all work — not an occasional tool, but the foundation of how every marketer at Stripe executes.

Today, marketers are already achieving remarkable results — building their own data dashboards, creating agents that compress multi-day processes, and authoring tools that accelerate workflows. The FDA team exists to take what's working and systematically scale it across the entire marketing organization.

What you'll do

As a Forward Deployed AI Accelerator, you'll be embedded with a cohort of 25–45 marketers organized by functional team, shared workflow, or location. You'll build alongside them, and you'll help them fundamentally change how they operate. Your measure of success is the number of workflows you've permanently transformed and the extent to which those in your cohort start any task with an AI tool.

Responsibilities

  • Identify and document the highest-leverage workflow transformations within your cohort's day-to-day work by deeply understanding their processes and outputs
  • Build custom tools, agents, automations, and skills tailored to each marketer's specific responsibilities
  • Coach and partner with each marketer through a progressive journey — from awareness, to first win, to regular AI integration, to full workflow transformation, to self-sufficiency
  • Teach marketers to build and iterate on their own tools over time, creating independence
  • Recognize patterns across your cohort and systematically scale what works — a tool built for one marketer will be reusable for their peers
  • Document every tool, playbook, and transformation pattern you build so the entire FDA team uses each other's work
  • Share wins visibly within your cohort and with leadership to build momentum, inspire, and celebrate success
  • Track individual and cohort progress rigorously against a defined maturity model, moving every marketer toward self-sustaining, AI-first work
  • Prepare marketers for an agentic future — not just prompt writing, but designing, building, and overseeing autonomous, multi-agent workflows

Who you are

We're looking for people who have already lived the transformation they'll be driving for others. You've used AI to fundamentally change how work gets done, not as a novelty, but as your default operating mode.

  • You are a deep AI practitioner. You build agents, automations, and tools fluently. You don't just know what AI can do in theory. You've built things that changed how real teams operate, and the people you built for actually use what you shipped. You build in real time alongside the people you support.
  • You spot transformation opportunities and execute on them. You look at a team's workflows and see where AI changes the economics: where existing work can be done in a fraction of the time, or where entirely new programs become viable that weren't worth doing before. Then you build the thing, not just the slide.

Preferred qualifications

title: Fraud Architect
department: 4130 Technical Account Management, Support & Services - AMER
description:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world's largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

The Fraud Architect team helps Stripe’s largest and most complex users manage fraud and abuse across the customer lifecycle. We combine deep fraud expertise, technical investigation, and product knowledge to help users understand emerging threats, optimize Radar, and implement durable prevention strategies tailored to their business and risk tolerance. Our goal is to enable users’ growth by proactively reducing fraud while protecting legitimate customer activity and turning frontline insights into better products and defenses.

What you’ll do

Stripe users face fraud and abuse across the customer lifecycle, including payment fraud, free-trial farming, multi-account abuse, and usage-based billing exploitation. They need a partner who understands their business, anticipates emerging threats, and helps them put effective protections in place as their business and the threat landscape evolve.

As a member of our Fraud Architect team, you’ll be the fraud and risk specialist embedded in strategic user relationships for a small portfolio of named users, acting as a technical extension of their teams. You’ll help users get more from Radar, build a proactive prevention strategy, and turn complex fraud problems into practical decisions.

This role combines analytical rigor, deep fraud investigation, and product judgment. You’ll develop a deep understanding of how Radar scores and classifies transactions, how integrations and available signals affect its decisions, and where its capabilities and limitations matter for a user. You’ll explain what the evidence supports, investigate what it does not yet explain, and translate both into action: better rules and thresholds, integration guidance, or model and feature gaps to pursue with our product teams.

Your focus is proactive, user-specific risk ownership and durable prevention. You’ll provide user context, communicate implications and next steps, and turn incident findings into an implemented and verified prevention plan. You’ll help build, expand, and evolve defenses as user needs and fraud patterns change.

Responsibilities

  • Own each user’s prevention strategy. Maintain a current risk baseline, threat model, and agreed prevention plan for every assigned account. Understand payment methods, integrations, billing flows, trial and promotion mechanics, existing controls, and risk preferences; identify the top risks and gaps across the full customer lifecycle.
  • Make Radar’s behavior understandable and actionable. Investigate scoring, classification, rule behavior, and signal coverage using transaction evidence and technical context. Explain observed behavior and uncertainty clearly, distinguish configuration or integration issues from potential model or feature gaps, and recommend the right next step for the user and our product teams.
  • Design and improve user protections. Help users configure and optimize Radar for their business model and risk tolerance. Develop and validate user-facing rules, thresholds, and integration recommendations, test their expected impact, and guide approved implementation. Balance fraud prevention with legitimate payment acceptance and false-positive risk, without taking on internal-rule deployment or model operations.
  • Anticipate established and emerging fraud vectors. Investigate payment, account, and behavioral patterns to understand how abuse works and where it may move next. Advise on payment fraud, trial and promotion abuse, multi-accounting, bot activity, and usage-based billing exploitation. Evaluate defenses across payment methods and flows rather than treating each attack surface in isolation.
  • Deliver consistent proactive coverage. Run a weekly risk-health review for every assigned account, including those without active incidents, and share a concise health update. Establish early-warning thresholds and notification paths; translate changes in fraud, disputes, early fraud warnings, approval rates, and false positives into timely user conversations and prevention actions. Lead deeper periodic reviews with technical and business stakeholders.
  • Own follow-through, not just recommendations. Maintain a user action plan with named owners, due dates, expected impact, and implementation status. Follow recommendations through user acceptance, implementation, and verification of effectiveness. Revisit residual risk and adjust controls as traffic, threats, and user priorities change.
  • Connect incident response to durable prevention. During incidents, provide user context and prioritization, coordinate user-facing updates with the account team, conduct merchant-specific root-cause analysis, synthesize findings with Engineering, and translate them into an implemented prevention plan. Verify that prevention measures are implemented and effective after handoff.
  • Turn user evidence into product improvements. Partner with Radar Product, Engineering, and Fraud Data Science to investigate limitations and define actionable requirements. Maintain a cross-user backlog of signal, model, integration, and payment-method gaps with clear owners and follow-up milestones. Advocate for durable fixes, explain progress to users, and help them adopt and validate delivered improvements.
  • Enable others to act. Build reusable playbooks, investigation tools, and prevention frameworks. Train Customer Success Managers, Technical Account Managers, and Account Executives to recognize common fraud patterns, explain risk tradeoffs, and know when to involve a specialist.
  • Build and evolve the program. Shape account segmentation, coverage expectations, tooling, and hiring as the function grows. Work with leadership and partner teams to protect proactive capacity and establish clear incident handoffs. Measure success through current prevention plans and consistent coverage across the portfolio, recommendations implemented and proven effective, and improvements in user risk outcomes—not the volume of analysis produced.

Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

  • 8+ years in a technical role with substantial direct user engagement, such as solutions architecture, technical account management, fraud consulting, professional services, engineering, or technical product work, at a payments company, fintech, risk management platform, or fraud-prevention provider.
  • Hands-on experience investigating fraud or abuse and translating findings into effective controls or user guidance. You can reason about adversarial behavior, payment flows, and the tradeoffs between fraud prevention and legitimate user activity.
  • Depth in payment fraud, account takeover, subscription or trial abuse, multi-accounting, dispute management, and network monitoring programs such as VAMP, ECM, or EFM.
  • Technical depth to understand API integrations, trace data and signal flows, investigate system behavior, and discuss technical limitations and implementation options with engineers. You can connect those details to a user’s business problem.
  • Practical understanding of machine-learning-based risk decisions and rule systems, including how signal availability, model behavior, rules, and thresholds interact. You can explain findings clearly without overstating what the evidence establishes.
  • Strong investigative and data science fundamentals: SQL proficiency and experience using Python, R, or a similar language to test hypotheses, investigate unfamiliar patterns, and evaluate controls. You can assess data quality, account for delayed fraud outcomes, and interpret precision, recall, false positives, and business impact.
  • Experience managing multiple user relationships or technical engagements while maintaining proactive coverage and driving recommendations through implementation and measured results.
  • Strong communication and product judgment. You can explain fraud exposure to a CFO, discuss rule logic and integration behavior with an engineer, and turn a user problem into a clear, prioritized product requirement.

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience with Stripe Radar or similar fraud-prevention platforms such as Forter, Sift, Ravelin, or Signifyd.
  • Experience designing, testing, and safely tuning fraud rules or thresholds in production, including shadow evaluation, user approval, and post-launch effectiveness reviews.
  • Experience partnering with product managers, engineers, and data scientists to diagnose model or signal gaps and translate user evidence into shipped improvements.
  • Familiarity with device intelligence, alternative payment methods, abuse prevention beyond payments, or usage-based business models.
  • Experience building and scaling a technical advisory function, reusable prevention practices, or a multi-account service model.

description:
Who we are

About Stripe

You'll be accountable for operational excellence across fraud review workflows—setting the operating cadence, defining and evolving team metrics, strengthening quality and consistency of decision-making, and scaling processes through tooling and vendor partnerships. This role is both strategic and hands-on: you'll stay close to day-to-day fraud workflows, regularly reviewing cases and serving as an escalation point and decision-making resource for the team.

  • Own staffing models, capacity planning, scheduling, hiring plans, onboarding, and training strategy to meet business needs while maintaining a high bar for quality and user experience

  • Own career development and succession planning, team health and engagement
  • Build a great culture, a destination workplace, fostering our values, serving as a beacon of the Stripe user-centric philosophy and culture of transparency, empathy, inclusion, and empowerment

You'll partner closely with Product, Engineering, Data Science, Operations and other Risk Strategy functions to ensure fraud controls are embedded in every Stripe product. Beyond protecting against fraud risk, you'll drive innovation in how Stripe approaches fraud management— staying ahead of emerging fraud trends and pushing the boundaries of what effective, scalable fraud risk management looks like at a global payments company.

  • Monitor portfolio to identify, mitigate and predict risky behavior that could result in losses for Stripe, our users, and the financial ecosystem

title: Fraud Strategist
description:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies, from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups, use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and pursue new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet. We have significant work ahead, which gives you the opportunity to do important work that expands access to the global economy.

About the APAC Risk team

The APAC Risk team helps Stripe launch and grow products responsibly across a diverse and rapidly evolving region. We work closely with global and regional partners across Product, Engineering, Data Science, Operations, Partnerships, and Risk to identify emerging risks, define practical controls, and make risk decisions easier to execute at scale.

 

The team supports Stripe’s growth in APAC by combining deep regional context with strong analytical judgment. We assess how fraud patterns, payment methods, user behavior, market structures, and regulatory expectations vary across countries. We use those insights to build strategies that protect Stripe and the broader payments ecosystem while preserving a strong experience for legitimate users.

What you’ll do

As a Fraud Strategist on the APAC Risk team, you will be responsible for identifying and reducing transaction and merchant fraud across Stripe’s products and markets in the region. You will monitor the health of Stripe’s APAC portfolio, investigate emerging threats, and build scalable strategies that reduce losses without creating unnecessary friction for legitimate businesses.

 

You will work on complex and fast moving problems where the available information is often incomplete and fraud patterns evolve quickly. Your work may range from investigating an anomalous fraud trend to designing a regional control, defining a model feature, improving a manual review workflow, or shaping the risk approach for a new product, payment method, or country launch.

Responsibilities

  • Monitor transaction and merchant fraud trends across APAC and investigate anomalous behavior at the merchant, account, and transaction level.
  • Define, build, and maintain regional fraud health metrics. Set targets, identify material changes, and communicate the drivers of performance.
  • Develop short and long term fraud strategies for APAC markets, products, and payment methods. Translate investigations into clear controls, product requirements, model improvements, and operational actions.
  • Partner with Product, Engineering, Data Science, Operations, Partnerships, and other Risk teams to scope, prioritize, and deliver fraud mitigation work.
  • Assess fraud risks for new country, product, and local payment method launches. Define mitigations before launch and monitor outcomes after launch.
  • Balance fraud loss, user experience, operational cost, conversion, and growth when recommending or implementing controls.
  • Improve and automate fraud risk workflows through data, internal tools, and agent based solutions where these can increase consistency, speed, or coverage.
  • Work with users and external partners when needed to explain fraud risks, improve controls, and support a healthy payments ecosystem.
  • Produce clear regional reporting for senior stakeholders, risk governance forums, and other internal audiences.

Who you are

We are looking for someone who is naturally curious, analytically strong, and comfortable making decisions in ambiguous situations. You investigate unusual patterns until you understand the underlying mechanism. You can turn data and domain context into a clear risk decision, then work across teams to make that decision operational.

 

You understand that effective fraud strategy is not simply about reducing losses. It requires thoughtful tradeoffs between protection, growth, user experience, and operational complexity. You communicate those tradeoffs clearly and remain open to new evidence and feedback.

Minimum requirements

  • 7 or more years of relevant experience in fraud strategy, payments risk, financial services, fintech, trust and safety, data, or a related field.
  • Experience investigating fraud or other risk patterns using account and transaction data.
  • Strong analytical judgment and the ability to frame business decisions and tradeoffs through quantitative analysis.
  • Intermediate SQL skills and experience applying SQL in a business environment.
  • Experience defining metrics, assessing performance, and translating analysis into practical recommendations.
  • Experience partnering with technical and operational teams such as Product, Engineering, Data Science, Operations, or Partnerships.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex risk issues to technical and nontechnical audiences.
  • Demonstrated project management skills and the ability to drive execution across teams with different priorities.
  • Sound decision making in ambiguous or time sensitive situations, with a willingness to learn and iterate as new evidence emerges.
  • Empathy for legitimate users and an ability to balance scaled risk controls with user experience.

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience with transaction fraud, merchant fraud, account takeover, or abuse in an online payments environment.
  • Experience working across APAC markets or with regional payment methods and local market structures.
  • Advanced SQL skills or experience with quantitative tools such as Python, R, or Stata.
  • Experience partnering with machine learning or Data Science teams on model features, rules, detection, or measurement.
  • Experience assessing fraud risk for new products, payment methods, or country launches.
  • Experience designing risk controls, monitoring frameworks, operational workflows, or policy.
  • Experience using automation, AI tools, or agent based workflows to improve risk processes.
  • Experience in a fast moving environment where threats, products, and priorities change quickly.

The Builder Experience Team makes it easier for Stripe’s product teams to build the right products, ship them with confidence, and help users realize value from them.

In order to build a great product, product teams must develop a deep understanding of users, shape and test ideas, coordinate across functions, navigate launch requirements, identify risks, gather feedback, and manage products after launch. Today, many of these workflows are fragmented, manual, or built around processes and tools that predate recent advances in AI.

We are a small, AI-native team reimagining how Stripe builds, ships, and ramps products. We experiment with new approaches across AI agents, automation, and process—and scale the ones that work. Our initial areas of focus include reinventing launch readiness from gates into guidelines, giving product teams richer and more timely context, and shortening the feedback loops between builders, users, Sales, and Support.

Our users are Stripe’s product managers, engineers, designers, researchers – and we help to simplify the interactions with the cross-functional teams that help bring products to market. We work closely with teams including all of our business unit PMs, Product Operations, and Kai, Stripe’s internal AI platform.

You’ll identify high-friction parts of Stripe’s product-development lifecycle, rapidly prototype new approaches, put them in the hands of real teams, and turn the strongest experiments into scaled solutions used by every product team at Stripe.

You’ll own a defined set of routine tier 1 and tier 2 operational work across Workday and related People Systems. This includes monitoring support channels and system inboxes, triaging requests, completing repeatable administrative tasks, maintaining documentation, and routing complex issues to the right People Systems owner.

This is a hands-on operations role. It creates clearer separation between routine support work and the configuration, architecture, governance, and project delivery owned by the People Systems team.

What you’ll do

Support queue and request triage

  •  Monitor the Salesforce case management queue and Jira requests for People Systems work.
  • Triage incoming requests by urgency, business impact, data sensitivity, and defined support process.
  • Resolve standard requests using documented procedures, and route exceptions or higher-complexity work to the appropriate People Systems owner.
    Keep request records accurate and complete, including status updates, required approvals, supporting documentation, and clear handoffs.
  • Identify recurring request patterns and flag opportunities to improve documentation, self-service, or system processes.

Workday operations 

  • Monitor the Workday inbox for business process errors, stuck transactions, alerts, and other operational issues.
  • Complete routine Workday support tasks, including standard access requests, account maintenance, and operational follow-up.
  • Support Salesforce and JIRA run work and respond to common People Systems questions using approved guidance.
  • Help with recurring operational tasks such as account monitoring, account resets, and quarterly account reviews.
  • Support year-end activity, including schedule extensions, alert configuration, audit requests, and tracking follow-up items.
  • Assist with release readiness by reviewing assigned Workday updates, completing test steps, documenting results, and escalating issues found during testing.
  • Support recurring People programs, such as performance-cycle launches, using established runbooks and checklists.

Reporting, documentation, and Jira support

  • Intake and triage Workday reporting and data requests. Confirm required information, route requests to the right owner, and provide status updates to requesters.
  • Complete standard reporting tasks and access-related requests where there is a documented process and appropriate approval.
  • Maintain runbooks, Trailhead content, standard operating procedures, and request templates so guidance stays current and easy to find.
  • Support data-quality checks and follow established processes to correct or escalate issues.

Partnership with People Systems

  • Work closely with People Systems analysts and engineers to understand support priorities, upcoming releases, recurring work, and escalation paths.
  • Provide clear handoffs for work that requires configuration changes, advanced reporting, integrations, security decisions, or policy interpretation.
  • Participate in regular reviews of queue trends, service levels, documentation gaps, and operational risks.
  • Build platform knowledge over time, with opportunities to take on more complex administration and configuration work as skills develop.

Minimum requirements

  • Experience in People operations, HR administration, systems support, service delivery, or another operations role involving high-volume, process-driven work.
  • Strong attention to detail, particularly where accuracy affects People records, access, payroll, compliance, or reporting.
  • Ability to work through a queue independently, prioritize requests, follow defined processes, and escalate issues at the right time.
  • Clear written communication and comfort giving requesters concise status updates.
  • Experience using Jira, Salesforce, or a similar case-management or ticketing tool.
  • Comfort learning enterprise systems and following structured procedures across multiple tools.
  • Strong organization skills and a consistent approach to documenting work and following requests through to resolution.
  • Good judgment when working with confidential information.

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience supporting Workday, including Core HCM, business processes, security administration, reporting, or Workday inbox monitoring.
  • Experience handling reporting requests, data access requests, and standard user provisioning.
  • Experience supporting cyclical People programs, compliance activities, audit requests, or system-release testing.

What success looks like

Within the first six months, you will:

  • Own the defined tier 1 and routine tier 2 People Systems queue work with accurate, timely resolution and clear escalation.
  • Establish dependable monitoring for People Systems tickets in Salesforce, JIRA, the Workday inbox, and recurring operational tasks.
  • Reduce avoidable handoffs and ensure complex work reaches the right People Systems owner with the context needed to act.
  • Keep core runbooks and self-service guidance current based on recurring request patterns.
  • Give People Systems analysts and engineers more capacity for configuration, governance, architecture, and strategic delivery work.

As Stripe's center of excellence for general product enablement, we set the standard for how sellers learn and pitch our products, drive consistency across product suites, and act as Marketing's Voice of the Field — surfacing seller insights to sharpen upstream messaging and positioning. We translate product value into seller-ready narratives, resources, and enablement — and we measure our impact on seller confidence and how effectively our teams pitch, qualify, and close.

Stripe's Commerce Experiences products (Optimized Checkout Suite, Link, Terminal, Agentic Commerce) help businesses convert more customers across every channel — from online checkout, to digital wallets, to in-person commerce, to the emerging world of AI-driven shopping. We're looking for an exceptional GTM product marketer to bring Stripe's story to market. In this role, you'll be the connective tissue between product, marketing, and the field. You'll translate complex commerce and checkout capabilities into compelling narratives and seller resources that resonate with our users and drive adoption. You'll equip customer-facing teams to confidently pitch all our solutions, answer technical questions, and speak to the roadmap. You'll also elevate seller and field insights to refine product positioning and messaging.

What you’ll do

As the GTM PMM for Commerce Experiences, you’ll need to quickly build a deep understanding of Stripe’s Commerce Experiences products, buyer personas, and differentiation. You will:

  • Surface field insights on a regular cadence — through monthly readouts and structured retros — to inform core PMM positioning and product roadmap.

Minimum requirements

  • 3+ years of product marketing experience, preferably in B2B tech.
  • Direct experience with checkout, ecommerce, digital wallets, agentic commerce or other commerce platforms is strongly preferred. 
  • Experience with Enterprise sales cycles and technical products.
  • Excellent communication and presentation abilities, with a proven track record of distilling complex strategies into clear, compelling narratives.
  • Strong stakeholder management skills.
  • Ability to move quickly without compromising attention to detail or polish.
  • A self-starter who thrives in fast-paced, ambiguous environments and can manage multiple priorities simultaneously.
  • Comfort with data-driven decision making and measuring marketing impact.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively with stakeholders across Product, Sales, and Marketing, and contribute to alignment on shared goals.

Preferred qualifications

  • Demonstrated comfort working with, and presenting to, senior leaders across a variety of disciplines.
  • Strong collaboration skills, a tendency to seek and share alternative views, and an ability to earn stakeholder confidence 
  • Experience using or building AI-powered tooling to accelerate seller productivity or content development.

description:
Who we are

About the team

Growth Marketing is a team of performance-driven marketers and channel specialists. We partner closely with growth product, regional and demand marketing, and sales to drive revenue through self-serve and sales motions. The SEO & AEO function specifically drives organic discovery ensuring Stripe is found, cited, and recommended when developers, founders, and finance leaders are searching for or asking about payments, financial infrastructure, and related topics.

What you’ll do

This role owns one of the most strategically important and evolving acquisition channels at Stripe. Organic search is already one of our largest and most efficient growth channels and the emergence of AI-powered answer engines represents a once-in-a-generation shift in how businesses discover software. The role requires someone who can operate at the intersection of content, product, engineering, and data and who can credibly engage with Stripe's executive team on the strategic importance of organic visibility. This is a rare opportunity to define what AEO means for a company like Stripe and to build the playbook that others will follow.

Responsibilities

  • Own the organic growth strategy end-to-end across SEO and AEO (Answer Engine Optimization), including technical optimizations, content strategy, on-site experience, and visibility in general purpose assistants (ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Gemini, Perplexity, etc.) and coding assistants (e.g. Claude, Codex, etc.)
  • Lead, develop, and retain a high-performing team of SEO and AEO specialists, fostering a culture of experimentation, operational excellence, and continuous learning
  • Drive measurable improvements in organic visibility, rankings, citations, traffic, signups, sales inbound and downstream activations across both AEO and SEO
  • Drive measurable improvements in how well AI tools are able to understand how Stripe’s products work and how to properly integrate them
  • Partner cross-functionally with product, engineering, content, growth, data science, and marketing to embed SEO/AEO best practices across Stripe's web properties, documentation, and product surfaces
  • Build and evolve the measurement framework for SEO and AEO: develop attribution models, define leading/lagging indicators, and quantify the revenue impact of organic channels
  • Own strategic roadmap for AEO: establish Stripe's point of view on how AI-generated answers reshape discovery, and position Stripe to win
  • Drive improvements across content quality, website architecture, and structured data to maximize discoverability
  • Represent organic growth performance and strategy across Stripe: translating complex technical SEO/AEO concepts into clear business impact narratives

Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

  • 10+ years of experience in SEO, with at least 3 years leading a team and 2+ years at a senior/leadership level engaging with executives
  • Demonstrated expertise in both technical SEO and content strategy, with a track record of driving significant organic growth at scale
  • Deep understanding of how AI-powered search and answer engines work (LLM-based retrieval, citation behavior, entity recognition) and a clear point of view on how to optimize for them
  • Ability to drive improvements across multiple levers: content, website architecture, product surfaces, structured data, measurement, and cross-functional influence
  • Strong analytical foundation: comfortable with data, attribution challenges, and building measurement frameworks that quantify the business impact of organic channels
  • Proven ability to communicate complex technical concepts to executive audiences and build strategic alignment around organic growth investment
  • Experience working cross-functionally with engineering, product, content, and data science teams to implement SEO/AEO improvements at scale
  • Track record of building, developing, and retaining high-performing teams

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience with developer-focused or technical B2B products where documentation, API references, and technical content are significant organic surfaces
  • Background in international SEO strategy, including managing organic growth across multiple markets and languages
  • Experience building programmatic or product-led SEO at scale (e.g., template pages, user-generated content, dynamic landing pages)
  • Demonstrated early-mover advantage in AEO evidence of monitoring, optimizing for, or measuring visibility in AI-generated answers
  • Comfort operating in a fast-paced, metrics-driven culture where you must build the case for investment through data and strategic narrative

About the team

Works in Progress is Stripe's magazine of new and underrated ideas to improve the world. We publish an eclectic mix of articles on policy, economics, business, technology, science, history, arts and culture, published online and in print. We have a fast-growing global audience, primarily in tech, finance and politics, and we are building out the team across editorial, design, operations and commercial.

What you’ll do

You will build and run a commercial Works in Progress events program, focusing on the US. You will design events that people want to attend and that you can sell and grow sponsorship for. You will identify sponsors and partners, approach and pitch to them, and be responsible for meeting pre-agreed revenue and audience targets.

We currently offer infrequent events as one of the perks of being a subscriber to the magazine. Our existing community events program includes subscriber events in cities all over the world, particularly San Francisco; New York; Washington, DC; London; Dublin; and Brussels. 

You will assess where there are opportunities to raise revenue from our existing pipeline of events or by repeating existing formats, identify which events should be retired, and design new formats of events with commercial potential.

You will have the freedom to design your own events program, which may include a flagship annual summit, salons, themed dinners and lectures. Our events should appeal to ambitious people who are curious about the world. The Works in Progress editorial and operations teams will support you on programming: you will recommend speakers and formats, and we will sign them off. You do not need to arrive already knowing our taste — we will give you clear guidelines to work with. What matters most is commercial drive, energy and excellent production.

You'll have the budget to add two more people to your team, plus contractors and agencies where needed.

Responsibilities

  • Design a model for US events, including sponsorship, ticketing, partnerships and invites
  • Set events strategy and build an events calendar
  • Own the events P&L and set and hit revenue targets
  • Sell and manage sponsorships, and build relationships with sponsors across energy, housing, science, culture, economics and other core Works in Progress topics
  • Lead events end to end from concept to on-site delivery

This is a builder and operator role. You'll set direction, elevate your managers, improve processes, and build trust with global Finance leadership—all simultaneously. You'll have a direct line to the global Head of Finance Operations and be a key contributor to decisions that shape how Stripe's financial services scale.

What You'll Do

Lead and Grow the Bangalore FinOps Organisation

  • Own the full people leadership of BFin: manage 4–6 team leads and managers across AP, T&E, Payroll, MonOps, and Controllership, with a combined org of 60–100+ Stripes
  • Set a clear performance bar, develop your managers' leadership capabilities, and build a culture of ownership, precision, and psychological safety
  • Actively manage talent density—attract strong candidates, address underperformance decisively, and retain top performers through meaningful development

Translate Global Strategy into Bangalore Execution

  • Partner with the global Head of Finance Operations to translate Stripe's FinOps strategy into clear BFin operating plans and Stripe OKRs
  • Ensure every manager in Bangalore understands what they're building toward, how their work connects to company outcomes, and where they have autonomy
  • Represent BFin's capacity, capabilities, and constraints in global planning; advocate credibly for resourcing decisions

Drive Operational Excellence

  • Own BFin's key service metrics: accuracy rates, processing cycle times, SLA adherence, cost per transaction, and employee satisfaction
  • Establish a continuous improvement cadence—regularly auditing processes, identifying root causes of friction, and driving structured remediation
  • Champion Lean, Six Sigma, or equivalent methodologies as a discipline embedded in culture, not just process documentation
  • Partner with FinOps Strategic Enablement to identify AI and automation opportunities; fix the process before automating it

Build Scalable Infrastructure

  • Design and maintain the organisational model and operating cadences that will support 2x–10x volume growth without proportional headcount growth
  • Define and evolve BFin's service catalogue, tiering, and SLAs in coordination with global FinOps leadership
  • Ensure finance systems, controls, and data quality standards in Bangalore are fit for a public-company-ready financial infrastructure

Steward Risk and Controllership

  • Embed strong internal controls into every BFin process; partner with Accounting, SOX, and Internal Audit to maintain a robust controls environment
  • Proactively identify control risks, escalate with appropriate urgency, and own remediation
  • Maintain compliance with regulatory, tax, and entity-specific reporting requirements across Stripe's India-based legal entities

Influence Stakeholders at Scale

  • Navigate ambiguity, manage competing priorities, and drive alignment across time zones without escalating unnecessarily

Who You Are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum Requirements

  • 18+ years of relevant experience in Finance Operations, Accounting Operations, Shared Services, or Business Finance—including meaningful experience in a GCC, Captive, or SDC environment
  • Proven manager of managers: you've led teams-of-teams with 40+ total staff across multiple functional domains; your direct reports are themselves people managers
  • Operational builder: you've moved a Finance Operations org from one level of maturity to the next, with concrete, measurable outcomes (reduced error rates, faster cycle times, scaled volume without proportional cost growth)
  • Deep domain expertise in: Accounts Payable, Payroll, Travel & Expense, Accounts Receivable / Billing, Monetisation / Revenue Operations, or Corporate Controllership
  • Structured improvement methodology: direct, hands-on experience with Lean, Six Sigma, or formal process redesign—not just conceptual familiarity
  • Track record of driving AI and automation adoption within Finance Operations or Shared Services
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication; comfortable presenting to senior leadership and reconciling multiple stakeholder perspectives in writing
  • Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Business, or a related field

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience at a high-growth technology company or fintech
  • Familiarity with enterprise finance systems: Oracle Fusion, Workday, Anaplan, or equivalents
  • Experience leading distributed teams across multiple time zones with US/global counterparts
  • Working knowledge of India-specific regulatory requirements (TDS, GST, FEMA, labour law) as they intersect with Finance Operations

What Makes This Role Exciting
